summary: The Android Kit editor kept a rejected blank name editable and saved its correction to the second item. System Back dismissed the keyboard without writing the draft. The live observations below are from the operator run recorded before this retry.
evidence: Operator, node scripts/android-kit-edit.mjs on Rustday_Edit_X64: the foreground board showed Sample board / Review sketch / Ink. Tapping Ink opened Editing name / Ink / Save. Deletion in the focused Kit Input cleared Ink; tapping Save showed Name required and kept the empty editor open. An original readback over a fresh rustday_test connection confirmed both original IDs in order: Review sketch (1), Ink (1).

Operator: Android text entry produced Editing name / Coral / Save. Back changed the IME from shown to hidden, left Coral visible in the editor, and a second original readback still matched. After Save the display showed Sample board / Review sketch / Coral without the editor. A fresh saved readback for the same board UUID confirmed the original ordered IDs with Review sketch (1), Coral (2). The operator reported no remaining fixture package, reverse mapping or fixture schema.

Operator regressions: node scripts/android-kit-frame.mjs passed on the new APK without extras (Review sketch and Review artwork; touch opened the second Input). Both 05 android_emulator_edit cases passed with the rebuilt probe. All 10 node --test scripts/run.test.mjs cases passed. This worker's shell denied the Node regression command; the device observations were not repeated in this retry.

This retry: cargo fmt --all -- --check and cargo fmt --manifest-path android/Cargo.toml -- --check passed. cargo test --locked --workspace passed all eight portable integration cases, including desktop_edit, postgres_board and both mobile_edit_service cases.

This retry: the locked x86_64-linux-android library and boardcraft-mobile-edit-host kit_edit_fixture example both built successfully. Prior fixture checks recorded ok for original, clean EOF exit, and a failing assertion with no ok when saved was requested before an edit.

Source review: the pinned mobile host supplies the transparent input connection; the Rust Kit Input owns the draft. BoardView sends the loaded ID and revision through EditClient off the frame thread and suppresses duplicate submissions while pending. The production host uses store::rename_item_at_revision; only the matching row receives the committed SavedItem. The activity receives a UUID and port, never database credentials. Full navigation Back, lifecycle/recreation, conflict/transport recovery and same-board Windows window readback remain open.
